illustrae.name: Educational molecular biology diagram showing the DNA replication fork. Flat vector. White background. Scientific textbook style. Arial or Verdana minimum 11pt.  OVERALL STRUCTURE — Y-SHAPED REPLICATION FORK: The diagram is oriented horizontally. On the far left: the parental double helix shown as two intertwined strands (right-handed B-form, clockwise twist — do NOT render left-handed helix). The double helix opens rightward into a Y-shape at the replication fork junction. The two unwound template strands extend to the upper right (leading strand template) and lower right (lagging strand template). Far left label at the double helix: 'Origin of Replication' with a leftward bracket or marker.  HELICASE: Place helicase at the exact fork junction — the point where the double helix separates into two single-stranded template arms. Show helicase as a ring-shaped or oval protein complex surrounding the DNA at the fork point. Label: 'Helicase — breaks hydrogen bonds at replication fork.' Do not place helicase anywhere else on the diagram.  SINGLE-STRANDED BINDING PROTEINS (SSBs): On both the upper and lower single-stranded template regions between helicase and DNA polymerase, show multiple small oval or rectangular protein shapes bound to the single-stranded DNA. Label: 'Single-Stranded Binding Proteins (SSBs) — stabilize unwound template.' SSBs must appear on BOTH template strands.  LEADING STRAND (upper arm of Y-fork): Template strand runs 3'→5' (right to left away from fork — this is the template being read). New leading strand synthesized 5'→3' toward the fork — continuously, no gaps. Show the new strand as a solid colored line being synthesized in one continuous piece. Show DNA Polymerase III (in prokaryotes) as a large oval protein complex at the growing end of the leading strand. Label: 'DNA Polymerase — Leading Strand synthesis (continuous).' Show a short RNA primer at the 5' initiation end of the leading strand. Label: 'RNA Primer.' Directionality arrow on leading strand pointing toward fork: '5' → 3'.'  LAGGING STRAND (lower arm of Y-fork): Template strand runs 5'→3' (away from fork — antiparallel to leading strand template). New lagging strand synthesized in Okazaki fragments — each fragment synthesized 5'→3' but in the direction AWAY from the replication fork. Show 3 to 4 Okazaki fragments as separate discontinuous segments on the lagging strand, each pointing away from the fork. Gaps visible between fragments. Each Okazaki fragment has a short RNA primer at its 5' end. Label one primer: 'RNA Primer.' Show one DNA Polymerase complex on the lagging strand actively synthesizing an Okazaki fragment. Label: 'DNA Polymerase — Lagging Strand synthesis (discontinuous).' Label the fragments: 'Okazaki Fragments — Prokaryotes: 1000–2000 nucleotides / Eukaryotes: 100–200 nucleotides.' Directionality arrows on lagging strand fragments pointing away from fork: '5' → 3'.' Label overall lagging strand direction: 'Lagging Strand — discontinuous synthesis.'  STRAND POLARITY SUMMARY: Add a small two-line annotation near the fork: 'Leading strand: synthesized continuously toward fork (5'→3')' 'Lagging strand: synthesized discontinuously away from fork (5'→3')'  PROOFREADING INSET (bottom right corner, inside clean bordered box): Inset header: 'DNA Polymerase Proofreading — 3' Exonuclease Activity' Show four sequential steps left to right: Step 1: Short double-stranded DNA segment. One mismatched base pair shown — incorrect base labeled 'Mismatched Base (X)' with a red X marker. Label: 'Step 1 — Mismatch incorporated.' Step 2: Same segment. DNA polymerase shown pausing/reversing direction. Label: 'Step 2 — Polymerase detects mismatch.' Step 3: The mismatched base being excised — show it being removed with a curved arrow pointing away from the strand. Label: 'Step 3 — 3'→5' exonuclease removes incorrect base.' Direction arrow: 3'→5' (this is the removal direction — opposite to synthesis). Step 4: Correct base inserted in place of the removed base. Synthesis arrow pointing 5'→3' resuming. Label: 'Step 4 — Correct base inserted. Synthesis resumes 5'→3'.'  REQUIRED LABELS (all):  'Origin of Replication' (far left) 'Helicase — breaks hydrogen bonds' (fork junction) 'Single-Stranded Binding Proteins (SSBs)' (both template arms) 'DNA Polymerase — Leading Strand (continuous)' (upper arm) 'DNA Polymerase — Lagging Strand (discontinuous)' (lower arm) 'RNA Primer' (leading strand + one Okazaki fragment) 'Okazaki Fragments — 1000–2000 nt (prokaryotes) / 100–200 nt (eukaryotes)' (lower arm) '5'→3'' directional arrows on both strands 'Leading Strand' and 'Lagging Strand' strand labels Inset: all four proofreading step labels  STYLE: Flat vector. White background. No 3D. No gloss. No drop shadows. Parental helix: dark navy. New leading strand: deep blue. New lagging strand / Okazaki fragments: deep teal. RNA primers: orange segments. SSB proteins: warm gray ovals. DNA Polymerase: purple oval complex. Helicase: green ring at fork. Font: Arial or Verdana minimum 11pt. Footer: 'Educational illustration only. illustrae.name:
Create a scientific medical illustration titled "Tumor Grade" showing four circular microscopy panels side by side, labeled Grade 1 through Grade 4, with a horizontal gradient arrow beneath them labeled from left to right: "Well differentiated → Moderately differentiated → Poorly differentiated → Undifferentiated."
All panels should use a hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining color palette: pale pink cytoplasm and purple/violet nuclei on a light pink background.

Grade 1 (Well Differentiated): Cells are elongated and organized in parallel rows, resembling normal tissue architecture. Nuclei are small, uniform, oval-shaped, and evenly spaced. Cell borders are clearly defined. Minimal nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio.
Grade 2 (Moderately Differentiated): Cells are rounder and less organized than Grade 1, losing the parallel arrangement. Nuclei are slightly larger and more variable in size and shape. Some loss of tissue architecture. Moderate nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio.
Grade 3 (Poorly Differentiated): Cells are predominantly round, densely packed, with significant loss of normal tissue structure. Nuclei are enlarged, irregular, and hyperchromatic (darker purple staining). High nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio. Prominent nucleoli may be visible.
Grade 4 (Undifferentiated): Cells are highly pleomorphic — highly variable in size and shape. Nuclei are very large, irregular, and intensely hyperchromatic, nearly filling the cell. Extreme nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio. Complete loss of normal tissue architecture. Some cells may appear multinucleated.

Style: Clean, professional biomedical textbook illustration. Flat vector or digital painting style. White background. Bold sans-serif labels. Circular panels with thin dark borders. Include a right-pointing arrow beneath all four panels spanning the full width."
